title: Model Static and Dynamic Infrastructure
objective: Separate environments, scope variables, and combine static and dynamic inventory sources.

sourceAlignment.title: Ansible for DevOps, 2nd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Jeff Geerling
sourceAlignment.note: Original companion material covering host_vars, group_vars, cloud plugins, add_host, group_by, and custom inventory.

paragraphs: Production inventories model application tiers and environments without embedding configuration procedure. Separate development, staging, and production sources reduce accidental cross-environment targeting.

host_vars stores host-specific facts and group_vars stores shared settings. Dynamic inventory plugins query cloud APIs such as AWS or DigitalOcean; constructed groups can classify returned hosts from tags and metadata.

Multiple sources can be combined. add_host and group_by create in-memory groups during a run, while a custom inventory must emit the documented JSON shape and support host details. Treat cloud credentials as secrets.
explanation.rule: Separate environments and derive dynamic groups from durable metadata, not fragile hostnames.

examples.title: Environment Groups
examples.code:
all:
  children:
    production:
      children:
        webservers:
        databases:
examples.note: A parent environment can contain application-tier child groups.

checks.question: Why use a dynamic inventory plugin?
options: To discover changing infrastructure from its source of truth

feedback.incorrect: Dynamic inventory queries a provider rather than relying on a stale host list.

assignment.title: Model Production Tiers
assignment.brief: Create production with webservers and databases as child groups.
requirements: Nest both tier groups beneath production children.
assignment.solutionCode:
all:
  children:
    production:
      children:
        webservers:
        databases:

hints: Production needs its own children key.
The two tiers align beneath that key.
